data.name: LOST ORBIT
data.detailed_description:
Stranded after his ship is destroyed in deep space, Harrison, a lowly maintenance worker and our hero, must struggle to find his way home...

LOST ORBIT: Terminal Velocity is out July 16, 2019
The definitive edition of LOST ORBIT and free to owners of this version!


LOST ORBIT centers around the exploration of space. Players take control of a lone astronaut (Harrison) who sets off on a dangerous journey to rejoin his civilization, armed with only an improvised set of equipment and a relentless spirit. Without the help of his ship, Harrison will need to use the gravitational forces of planets to navigate and propel himself through space.

Set in a world rich with comedy and tragedy, LOST ORBIT is a game filled with risk, loneliness, wonder, and death.


Features:
  • Explore 40 levels set across 4 unique solar systems on your perilous journey home.
  • Each level features a detailed ranking system and time trial mode.
  • Choose and upgrade your set of abilities to customize Harrison as you see fit through a light RPG system.
  • Boost, swim, bounce, leap and teleport your way through a myriad of obstacles.
  • Simple and intuitive controls make the game easy to pick up, yet surprisingly deep.
  • Balanced between tense technical moments and cathartic graceful flight, LOST ORBIT is a game that is instantly immersive and satisfying to play.
  • Die alone in space; where no one will know of your struggle.

reviews.review:
LOST ORBIT is an imaginative science-fiction action adventure that turns the struggle for survival in deep space into a thrilling journey of speed, precision, and determination. Developed and published by PixelNAUTS, the game follows Harrison, a maintenance worker stranded far from civilization after the destruction of his spacecraft. With no functioning ship to carry him home, he must navigate dangerous cosmic environments using his personal equipment, gravitational forces, and quick reflexes. The premise is straightforward but compelling, offering an unusual perspective on space exploration that emphasizes vulnerability and resourcefulness rather than powerful spacecraft or elaborate combat systems.

The gameplay revolves around guiding Harrison through hazardous environments while maintaining momentum and avoiding deadly obstacles. Unlike conventional space adventures, the experience focuses on movement rather than combat or resource gathering. Players must carefully control acceleration, direction, and positioning while navigating increasingly complicated routes. Boosting through open space creates an exhilarating sensation of freedom, but excessive speed can quickly become dangerous when obstacles appear. This balance between caution and aggressive movement forms the foundation of the experience, rewarding players who develop precise control and learn to anticipate environmental hazards.

One of the game's strongest features is its collection of movement abilities. Harrison can boost, swim, bounce, leap, and teleport, providing several methods for overcoming obstacles. These mechanics introduce variety and encourage experimentation, particularly when combined with gravitational interactions that can dramatically influence movement. Mastering these techniques produces satisfying moments where complicated sections can be completed through carefully timed maneuvers. However, the controls demand practice, and mistakes can result in repeated failures. Players who appreciate challenging arcade experiences will likely enjoy this learning process, while those seeking a more forgiving adventure may occasionally find it frustrating.

The campaign features 40 levels across four solar systems, providing a structured progression through different cosmic environments. Each stage challenges players to refine their skills while adapting to new hazards and increasingly demanding obstacle arrangements. The level design encourages repeated attempts and rewards familiarity with movement mechanics. Although the setting suggests expansive space exploration, the actual experience follows carefully constructed routes rather than offering unrestricted freedom. This focused approach allows the game to maintain consistent pacing, although players expecting an open-world adventure may find its structure somewhat restrictive.

A lightweight upgrade system adds another dimension to the gameplay by allowing players to improve Harrison's abilities. These enhancements provide a sense of progression while supporting different approaches to navigation. The system is relatively simple and does not offer extensive character customization, but it complements the central mechanics without introducing unnecessary complexity. Meanwhile, the ranking system and time trials encourage replayability by rewarding efficient movement and faster completion times. Returning to earlier levels to improve performance can be satisfying, especially when previously difficult sections become manageable through experience.

The narrative provides an unexpectedly personal element to the adventure. Harrison is not a legendary explorer or fearless warrior, but an ordinary individual determined to survive an extraordinary situation. His journey home establishes an emotional motivation that makes the challenges feel meaningful. A sarcastic robotic companion introduces humor and personality, creating entertaining contrasts with the isolation and danger of deep space. Although the storytelling remains relatively modest, its combination of determination, loneliness, and occasional comedy gives the experience a distinctive identity.

Visually, LOST ORBIT presents a colorful interpretation of the cosmos, combining attractive celestial environments with dangerous obstacles. The artistic direction emphasizes atmosphere and movement rather than photorealistic detail. Traveling rapidly through vibrant environments creates an appealing sense of momentum, while quieter passages provide opportunities to appreciate the surrounding scenery. The soundtrack and sound effects complement this presentation, reinforcing both the wonder of space travel and the tension of navigating hazardous areas. However, certain visually busy sequences can make obstacles difficult to anticipate, particularly when moving at high speeds.

The main drawbacks involve difficulty, repetition, and limited gameplay variety. Because the experience relies heavily on obstacle avoidance, some sections can begin to feel familiar despite the introduction of additional mechanics. Repeated deaths may interrupt the flow, especially during demanding sequences requiring precise timing. Nevertheless, these challenges also contribute to the satisfaction of mastering difficult stages. The game is most enjoyable when approached with patience and an appreciation for skill-based progression rather than expectations of extensive exploration or complex storytelling.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, the original LOST ORBIT currently has an Unknown classification, meaning it has not received an official Verified or Playable designation. Its full controller support suggests that handheld gameplay could be practical, although actual performance and compatibility have not been officially confirmed. The expanded edition, LOST ORBIT: Terminal Velocity, has a separate Playable classification on Steam Deck, making it worth considering for handheld players.

Overall, LOST ORBIT succeeds by combining responsive movement, creative environmental challenges, and atmospheric storytelling into an enjoyable arcade adventure. Its emphasis on precision and momentum creates a rewarding experience for players willing to practice and improve. Despite occasional frustration and a somewhat repetitive structure, its distinctive mechanics, colorful presentation, and engaging progression make it a worthwhile journey through the dangers of deep space.

A creative and challenging space adventure that delivers satisfying movement mechanics, memorable atmosphere, and rewarding gameplay for players who enjoy precision-based action.

Rating: 8/10
